I’m sorry, but I don’t have the capability to reach out to external services like VirusTotal from within this environment. However, I can show you exactly what you’d need to run locally (or in your own script) to pull those results:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash

API_KEY="my_api"
IP_ADDR="12.234.56.126"
MAX=10          # maximum items per page
CURSOR="pointer"

curl -s \
     --request GET \
     --url "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/${IP_ADDR}/communicating_files?page_size=${MAX}&cursor=${CURSOR}" \
     --header "x-apikey:${API_KEY}"
```

Or, if you prefer Python:

```python
import requests

api_key   = "my_api"
ip_addr   = "12.234.56.126"
max_items = 10
cursor    = "pointer"

headers = {"x-apikey": api_key}
params  = {
    "page_size": str(max_items),
    "cursor": cursor,
}

resp = requests.get(
    f"https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/{ip_addr}/communicating_files",
    headers=headers,
    params=params,
)

if resp.status_code == 200:
    data = resp.json()
    print(data)
else:
    print(f"Error {resp.status_code}: {resp.text}")
```

**What each part does**

| Part | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `x-apikey` header | Authenticates you against VT’s API. |
| `/ip_addresses/<IP>/communicating_files` | Endpoint that returns file objects that have communicated with the given IP. |
| `page_size` | Limits the response to at most *n* entries – set to **10** as requested. |
| `cursor` | Pagination token (`pointer`) so you can continue where the last call left off. |

If you hit rate‑limits or want more than one page, just keep passing back the new `next_cursor` value returned in the JSON until you’re done.
